title: USF-171 Static Analysis Quality-Gate Disposition Matrix

humanDecision.summary: SonarQube/static-analysis decision is not completion evidence. USF-171 records a bounded disposition gate: local deterministic repository verification is mandatory but not SonarQube service equivalence. USF-195 records the explicit deferred service-proof boundary, while actual composed SonarQube scan and operator proof remains tracked by USF-204.

sonarqubeDisposition.riskStatement: SonarQube service semantics, unresolved issue handling, security hotspot treatment, and quality-gate exception workflow could be overclaimed from local repository verification output.
sonarqubeDisposition.treatment: record SonarQube service-semantic proof boundary in USF-195, defer actual composed scan and operator proof to USF-204, and keep local deterministic checks non-equivalent
deferredEvidence: quality-gate threshold and exception handling evidence
operator console access and audit evidence

localVerificationGate.substitutionNonEquivalenceBoundary: Repository validation commands are mandatory local deterministic verification evidence, but they are not equivalent to SonarQube service history, dashboards, issue lifecycle, security hotspot workflow, or quality-gate operations.

operatorAccessAuditRetentionSupplierBoun.operatorAccessBoundary: SonarQube operator console access remains defined-only under USF-195 and must be proven by USF-204 before a service readiness claim.
operatorAccessAuditRetentionSupplierBoun.retentionBoundary: No scanner findings or source-analysis payloads are retained in repository evidence by USF-171.
operatorAccessAuditRetentionSupplierBoun.secretBoundary: No SonarQube token, scanner credential, raw endpoint, or provider payload is introduced by USF-171.
operatorAccessAuditRetentionSupplierBoun.supplierBoundary: Local generated Compose service is not supplier/live-provider evidence; supplier posture is required before live-provider or production claims.
operatorAccessAuditRetentionSupplierBoun.incidentBoundary: No production incident or vulnerability-response workflow is proven by USF-171 or USF-195.
